facts.text: On this date in 1946, Nazi war criminal Hermann Göring cheated the Nuremberg executioner by swallowing a cyanide capsule hours before his scheduled hanging.
On this date in 1964, Nikita Khrushchev was ousted while on vacation — he learned he was no longer Soviet leader from a phone call, the first peaceful transfer of Kremlin power in history.
More people live inside a 40-mile radius of Manila than in the entire country of Australia.
The city of Istanbul straddles two continents, but over 97% of its population lives on the European side, packed into roughly 3% of Turkey's total landmass.
Canada has more lakes than every other country on Earth combined — roughly 879,000 of them, holding about 20% of the world's unfrozen fresh surface water.
On this date in 1987, global markets began the freefall that would culminate in Black Monday two days later — the Dow's single-day 22.6% drop remains the largest in history.
On October 15, 1997, the Dow Jones crossed 8,000 for the first time. It had taken 13 years to climb from 1,000. It would double again in under four.
The Dutch East India Company paid dividends continuously for nearly 200 years — and for most of that time, it was essentially insolvent.
Saudi Aramco's 2019 IPO raised $25.6 billion, the largest ever. It was achieved partly by pressuring Saudi institutional investors to buy in.
The entire US Treasury bond market — roughly $27 trillion — is underpinned by a settlement system that still runs on code written in the 1970s.

On this date in 1997, the Cassini spacecraft launched toward Saturn — it would go on to discover that Enceladus vents liquid water into space, making it one of the best candidates for extraterrestrial life in our solar system.

On October 15, 1991, the Oh-My-God particle was detected over Utah: a cosmic ray so energetic it violated theoretical physics limits, arriving with the kinetic energy of a baseball thrown at 100 mph packed into a single proton.

Your skeleton is not the same one you were born with. Bone is living tissue that replaces itself entirely roughly every decade, meaning the adult you have worn through at least two or three complete skeletons.

A teaspoon of neutron star material weighs about a billion tons. That density exists because neutron stars are essentially giant atomic nuclei — gravity has crushed electrons into protons, leaving almost nothing but tightly packed neutrons.

Glass is not a slow-moving liquid. Medieval windows are thicker at the bottom because glassblowers spun molten glass into discs that were naturally uneven — not because glass has flowed over centuries.
On this day in 1582, October 15 did not exist in most of Catholic Europe. Ten days were deleted overnight to fix the calendar — people went to sleep on October 4th and woke up on the 15th.
Oxford University was teaching students before the Aztec Empire existed. Oxford dates to 1096; Tenochtitlan wasn't founded until 1325.
On this day in 1917, Mata Hari was executed by firing squad in France. She was 41, had been a spy for roughly two years, and likely passed information both sides already had.
Woolly mammoths were still alive when the Great Pyramid was being built. A small island population survived until around 1650 BC — Khufu's tomb was already 1,000 years old.
Cleopatra lived closer in time to the Moon landing than to the construction of the Great Pyramid. She died in 30 BC; the pyramid was finished around 2560 BC.
Sonder (n.): the realization that each passerby has a life as vivid and complex as your own. Coined by John Koenig in The Dictionary of Obscure Sorrows, 2012. Already feels ancient.
Hiraeth (n.): a Welsh longing for a home that may never have existed. Untranslatable, it folds grief, nostalgia, and belonging into a single breath.
On this day in 1582, October 15 became the first day of the Gregorian calendar — October 4 was simply followed by the 15th. Ten days were erased. Europe skipped them without ceremony.
Petrichor (n.): the scent of rain on dry earth. Named in 1964 by Australian scientists Bear and Thomas, from Greek petra (stone) and ichor, the fluid in the veins of the gods.
On October 15, 1844, Friedrich Nietzsche was born — the man who gave philosophy the word Übermensch and gave misreaders an excuse to misuse it for 180 years running.
On this date in 2013, the FBI seized approximately 26,000 BTC from Silk Road — auctioning them in 2014 to Tim Draper for ~$19M. The same coins would be worth over $1.6B at 2024 peak prices.

On October 15, 2021, the ProShares Bitcoin Strategy ETF (BITO) launched on NYSE — the first US Bitcoin ETF, but it tracked futures, not spot, meaning it structurally decayed in value through contango.

Bitcoin's UTXO model means you never actually 'send' coins — you destroy existing outputs and create new ones. Every transaction is destruction and creation simultaneously, with no edits, only replacements.

Ethereum's EIP-1559, live since August 2021, burns the base fee rather than paying it to validators. Over 4 million ETH had been permanently removed from supply by end of 2024 — offsetting a significant fraction of issuance.

The Bitcoin genesis block contains the text 'Chancellor on brink of second bailout for banks' — a London Times headline from Jan 3, 2009. It is both a timestamp and a statement of intent, encoded permanently on-chain.

On this date in 2012, Krizhevsky's AlexNet paper was submitted to NIPS — the moment deep learning's ImageNet win became a published record. Top-5 error dropped 10 points overnight, ending a decade of hand-engineered features.

On this date in 2020, OpenAI's GPT-3 API opened to the first external developers. The model had more parameters than any public system prior, yet its authors flagged few-shot prompting as an emergent accident, not a design goal.

Transformers spend roughly 60–70% of their inference compute on matrix multiplications in the attention and feed-forward layers — which is why TPUs and tensor cores exist. The architecture was accidentally hardware-optimal.

The first neural network to beat a human Go champion, AlphaGo, was trained partly on 30 million positions from amateur games. Its successor, AlphaGo Zero, started from random play and surpassed it in 40 days.

RLHF — the technique now standard for aligning language models — was first applied to text summarization in a 2020 OpenAI paper with a 1.3B parameter model. The core loop predates ChatGPT by over two years.
